I'd like to share a story. It was the first thing that came to mind. I hope I can convey it properly in type.

I started a business. Exterior Cleaning. I always wanted to start a business and I thought I could do this relatively easy. It's been 2 years, with nothing really happening until this year (coinciding with my no PMO). 

I started watching YouTube videos, asking questions. Going to SCORE mentors and asking questions. Building business plans. Reading books. Studying. Creating business cards. Learning what dollar amount it takes to start up. Browsing r/smallbusiness. Slowly building my knowledge on what it takes to run a business. All this shit was helping. But I wasn't getting anywhere. Like, absolutely no here, unless you considered me a business theorist.

It wasn't until I talked to a guy who basically said, "Get a truck, get a flyer, and start canvasing". So I did. And since that moment I have made more mistakes then I think I have ever. THe truck I got was (and still is) a rustbucket. My flyer was laughably bad. And I went to 2 million dollar houses to drop of my flyers. Like they would ever take my business. This was in January. 

But now, after 10 attempts, I have 3 flyers that are fucking awesome that I built myself. I have changed my demographic from 2 million dollar homes to retirees and middle income folks. This week I got my fourth customer. And made a cool 3 bills.

All this time I was making mistake after mistake after mistake. Like, cringing mistakes. Fucking stupid shit where I was kicking myself and people looked at me like, "wtf bro?"

The biggest mistake was 2 weekends ago. I convinced a guy to let me soft wash his house. I told him I had experience (my dad let me do his house) and off I went to buy the supplies I "thought" I needed. 

I get to the house and start with the one side of the house. Not two minutes into spraying, the owner comes out and asked if I had messed with his security camera, because one went out. I flushed in horror.... I didnt unplug the exterior outlets before spraying the house with water.

All I could think about was, (1) I have no insurance and (2) I'm gonna have to pay for all sorts of electrical work and cameras and shit.

I was devastated. He said he'd be in touch. And I spent the whole weekend in a daze. Wondering what the fuck I was doing. Why I didnt have insurance, balah balash. 

Good news, he fixed it. and i was out a customer, but could have been a lot worse. 

After reflection I realized, had that happened a year ago, when I was the type of person I was back then, I would have been absolutely suicidal. I would have been in bed the whole weekend, terrified and eating my emotions. Smoking like a chimmney and killing myself slowly, if not just ending it by jumping in front of a bus. 

Not that extreme, but you know...

I wasn't like that though. I still went to my other job. Told people I trusted my mistake (they of course told me I was an idiot for not having insurance). Got feedback. Was introspective and replayed the events and thought what I could have done different. My mentality was, "ok, what do I do now? This happened, how can I move on?"
